 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• The HDI is a summary measure for assessing long-term progress in three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life (life expectancy), access to knowledge (education), and a decent standard of living (income).
 
• It was introduced by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in 1990.
 
• Countries are ranked on a scale from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating higher human development.
 
• The HDI is used to compare the level of development of different countries and to assess the impact of economic policies on quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Significance of HDI Rankings:**
 
 
• High HDI rankings indicate countries with higher life expectancy, better education systems, and higher income per capita.
 
• Countries with lower HDI rankings may face challenges such as poverty, poor healthcare, and inadequate education.
 
• Policies aimed at improving healthcare, education, and income distribution can help improve a country's HDI ranking.
 
 
 
• **Implications for Policy:**
 
 
• Governments use HDI rankings to identify areas that need improvement and to allocate resources more effectively.
 
• International organizations and donors also use HDI data to target development assistance and to monitor progress.
 
• Higher HDI rankings can attract foreign investment and improve a country's global standing.
